title: Stability of a Gauss-valued rational function field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. Let $n\ge1$ and let $P=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ be the ring of finite sums $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^n}a_
u X^
u$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Put $R=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$ and equip it with the Gauss absolute value $$\left| rac{f}{g}ight|_R= rac{\max_
u|f_
u|}{\max_
u|g_
u|}\qquad(f,g\in P,\ g
e0).$$ Then $R$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]: every finite extension $E/R$, endowed with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{E/R}$, has an $R$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ satisfying $$s_{E/R}\left(\sum_i a_iv_iight)=\max_i |a_i|_R s_{E/R}(v_i)\qquad(a_i\in R).$$ Neither completeness of $R$ nor separability of $E/R$ is assumed.

proof.text: First verify the Gauss absolute value. For nonzero polynomials $f,g$, divide each by a coefficient of maximum absolute value. Both normalized polynomials have coefficients of norm at most $1$ and nonzero reductions over $\widetilde k$. Their product reduction is nonzero: lexicographically largest monomials in their finite supports multiply to a unique largest monomial with nonzero coefficient. Thus the normalized product has Gauss norm $1$, proving $G(fg)=G(f)G(g)$. The coefficient inequalities give definiteness, $G(1)=1$, $G(-f)=G(f)$ and $G(f+g)\le\max(G(f),G(g))$. For fractions, $ad=bc$ implies $G(a)G(d)=G(b)G(c)$, so the displayed quotient is independent of representatives. Multiplication follows by taking products of numerators and denominators; for addition use $G(ad+bc)\le\max(G(a)G(d),G(b)G(c))$ and divide by $G(b)G(d)$. Constants have their original absolute values, so the extension is nontrivial.

source.place: Sections 5.1.2 and 5.3.3; finite coefficient/reduction calculation written out here.

proof.text: We first prove the claim under the extra assumption that $\Gamma=|k^\times|$ is divisible, meaning $r^{1/j}\in\Gamma$ for $r\in\Gamma$ and $j\ge1$. Let $E/R$ be any finite extension, $s=s_{E/R}$ and $d=[E:R]$. A nonzero Gauss value on $R$ belongs to $\Gamma$. In the minimal-polynomial formula for $s(z)$ at $z\ne0$, the finite maximum is a nonzero $|a_i|_R^{1/i}$, hence also belongs to $\Gamma$. Write $D=\widetilde E=\{s\le1\}/\{s<1\}$ and $F=\widetilde k$. By [lem-trf-spectral-reduction-dimension-criterion], $D$ is a nonzero finite reduced algebra over $\widetilde R$ and $\dim_{\widetilde R}D\le d$. Coefficient reduction identifies $\widetilde R$ with $F(X)$: normalize a denominator to Gauss norm $1$, reduce numerator and denominator, and note that the reduction vanishes precisely when the numerator has norm less than $1$; conversely lift the finitely many coefficients of any fraction in $F(X)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/3, printed pp.215–216: divisible-value-group case and equations (1)–(2).

proof.text:
Give $R$ also the independent total-degree absolute value $|f/g|_t=\exp(\deg f-\deg g)$. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $k[X]$ in $E$ and $B(
u)=\{z\in B:s_t(z)\le\exp(
u)\}$. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $F[X]$ in $D$ and define $C(
u)$ with its total-degree spectral norm. By [lem-trf-degree-filtration-rank-asymptotic], both filtrations have finite-dimensional pieces and $$d=n!\lim
u^{-n}\dim_k B(
u),\qquad \dim_{F(X)}D=n!\lim
u^{-n}\dim_F C(
u).$$ Apply [lem-trf-gauss-spectral-coefficient-cartesian] to the finite $k$-subspace $B(
u)\subset E$. Its restricted Gauss spectral norm admits an orthogonal $k$-basis. Step 2 gives its nonzero norm values in $\Gamma$, so [lem-trf-spectral-reduction-dimension-criterion] yields $\dim_F\widetilde{B(
u)}=\dim_kB(
u)$. The injective map of [lem-trf-gauss-degree-filtration-reduction] gives $\dim_kB(
u)\le\dim_FC(
u)$. Multiplying by $n!
u^{-n}$ and passing to the displayed limits gives $d\le\dim_{F(X)}D$. With Step 2 this is equality. The last clause of [lem-trf-spectral-reduction-dimension-criterion] supplies an orthonormal $R$-basis of $E$. This proves stability when $\Gamma$ is divisible, without imposing separability.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/3, equations (1)–(4), printed pp.216–217; Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed pp.216–218.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $|k^\times|$. By [lem-trf-completed-algebraic-closure-cartesian], choose the completed algebraic closure $k'$ with its extending absolute value; it is complete, algebraically closed and every finite $k$-subspace of it has an orthogonal $k$-basis. Algebraic closedness implies stability: every finite extension equals $k'$ and the basis $(1)$ has the equality in [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. It also implies divisibility of $|k'^\times|$, by taking roots of each nonzero element. Therefore Steps 2–3, applied with coefficient field $k'$, prove that $R'=k'(X)$ with its Gauss absolute value is stable. The inclusion $R\subset R'$ is isometric by the coefficient formula of Step 1.

source.place: Section 5.3.4, opening paragraph, printed p.218 (scan PDF p.224).

proof.text:
Every finite-dimensional $R$-subspace $U\subset R'$ is contained, after multiplication by a single nonzero polynomial $h\in k'[X]$, in the $R$-span of finitely many polynomials $u_j\in k'[X]$. Their coefficients span a finite $k$-subspace $V\subset k'$. Step 4 supplies an orthogonal $k$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $V$. For polynomials $f_i=\sum_
u a_{i
u}X^
u\in k[X]$, coefficientwise orthogonality gives $$G(\sum_i f_iv_i)=\max_
u|\sum_i a_{i
u}v_i|=\max_{i,
u}|a_{i
u}||v_i|=\max_iG(f_i)|v_i|.$$ A common denominator in $k[X]$ and multiplicativity of the Gauss absolute value give the same equality for $f_i\in R$. Hence $W=\sum_i Rv_i$ has that finite orthogonal $R$-basis and contains $hU$. By [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace-scalar-tower](1), $hU$ has an orthogonal basis. Dividing its vectors by $h$ gives one for $U$, because $|h^{-1}z|=|h|^{-1}|z|$. Thus every finite $R$-subspace of $R'$ is orthogonally based. This proves the constant-extension comparison explicitly; it is not an assumption that $R'$ is finite over $R$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.4/1, printed p.219 (scan PDF p.225): common denominator and coefficient-maximum computation.

proof.text: Fix a finite extension $E/R$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $R'$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], embed $E$ over $R$ into $\Omega$. Choose an $R$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of its image and put $A=\sum_iR'e_i\subset\Omega$. This is a finite-dimensional unital $R'$-subalgebra, since products $e_ie_j$ have their $R$-coordinates in the same basis. For $0\ne a\in A$, multiplication by $a$ is injective on the finite-dimensional space $A$, hence surjective; its image contains $1$, so $a^{-1}\in A$. Thus $E'=A$ is a finite field extension of $R'$ containing the image of $E$. By Step 4, its spectral norm $N=s_{E'/R'}$ has an orthogonal $R'$-basis. Step 5 and [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace-scalar-tower](2) imply that every finite $R$-subspace of $E'$, in particular $E$, has an orthogonal $R$-basis for the restricted norm $N|_E$.

source.place: Section 5.3.4, printed pp.218 and 220 (scan PDF pp.224 and 226): compositum and cartesian scalar restriction.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], $N|_E$ is an $R$-algebra norm (the Gauss inclusion is isometric). By [lem-trf-spectral-reduction-dimension-criterion], $N$ and its restriction are power-multiplicative. If $w_i$ is the orthogonal $R$-basis just obtained, set $c=\min_iN(w_i)>0$ and $C=\max_iN(w_i)>0$. Its equality implies $$c\max_i|a_i|_R\le N(\sum_i a_iw_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|_R.$$ Thus [lem-trf-product-topology-spectral-uniqueness] applies over $R$, despite its possible incompleteness, and gives $N|_E=s_{E/R}$. The same basis is therefore orthogonal for the required spectral norm. Since $E/R$ was arbitrary this is precisely stability in [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field].
